claims.text: Equimolar CoCrFeNiTi has a nearly ideal lattice with minimal local lattice distortion.
The starting CoCrFeNiTi solid solution lacks short-range chemical order.
The starting alloy lacks intrinsic nanoscale obstacles such as precipitates or twins.
Minimal lattice distortion and the absence of nanoscale obstacles permit easy, unimpeded dislocation glide.
The starting alloy undergoes rapid or efficient dynamic recovery during deformation.
Easy dislocation glide and dynamic recovery limit strain hardening and cause the low yield strength and hardness.
Conventional casting and homogenization can produce equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi as a single-phase simple solid solution.
This single-phase CoCrFeNiTi state has high plasticity and good machinability.
Cold working will introduce a high dislocation density in CoCrFeNiTi.
A short low-temperature anneal after cold working can pin dislocations or promote slight short-range ordering without forming a secondary phase.
Processing-induced dislocation structures or short-range order will impede subsequent dislocation motion.
The thermomechanically processed alloy will have greater yield strength and hardness than the untreated alloy.
The thermomechanically processed alloy will have a higher work-hardening rate than the untreated alloy.
Processed samples will exhibit more tangled or pinned dislocations than untreated samples.
Greater dislocation pinning will reduce dynamic recovery and thereby strengthen the alloy.
Subtle chemical fluctuations or weak short-range order may already act as obstacles in the starting material.
Twinning may contribute to deformation under the proposed testing conditions.
A deformation-induced phase transformation may contribute under the proposed testing conditions.
The proposed comparison is restricted to equimolar CoCrFeNiTi in a single-phase state under room-temperature, quasi-static uniaxial loading.
Failure of the treatment to produce both statistically significant strengthening and altered dislocation patterns would falsify the proposed mechanism.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis asserts an absence of short-range order, whereas the uncertainty field allows that weak short-range order may already exist and act as an obstacle.
The hypothesis includes the absence of twins among the reasons for unobstructed glide, but the uncertainty field states that a contribution from twinning has not been excluded.
